accuracy.evidence: Wording follows AQA A-level Chemistry 3.3.13 Amino acids, proteins and DNA ('amino acids have both acidic and basic properties, including the formation of zwitterions') and OCR A 6.2.2 (general formula RCH(NH2)COOH, systematic naming). IUPAC names checked: glycine 2-aminoethanoic acid, alanine 2-aminopropanoic acid, serine 2-amino-3-hydroxypropanoic acid. Alanine pKa values 2.34 and 9.69 (pI 6.0) match Lehninger; the hydrogen count 2n+5 for an unbranched alkyl R gives C3H7NO2 for alanine.

misconceptions.evidence: The lab refuses the classic A-level slips with a named reason: the NH2 placed two carbons from COOH is called out as a beta-amino acid, HO in place of H2N becomes a hydroxy acid, ethanoic for alanine is refused because the COOH carbon was not counted, 1- and 3-amino numbering is refused because C1 is the COOH carbon, glycine called chiral is refused (two H atoms), and the zwitterion chosen at pH 1 is refused because COO- gains H+.

lab_distinct.evidence: Mechanism is molecular assembly on one tetrahedral centre: four empty bonds on the alpha-carbon filled from six fragment chips (NH2, COOH, H, CH3 plus decoys OH and CHO), a name picker driven by the R group, a four-molecule chirality test, and a continuous pH slider whose species are computed from pKa 2.34 and 9.69. It shares no task with flagamine (amines as bases) and passed the 30% shingle gate against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Students discover each rule by acting first: assembling alanine from chips shows that NH2, COOH, H and R all hang off a single carbon; sliding pH from 0 to 14 shows cation, then zwitterion, then anion appear with the colour bands at the two pKa values; tapping glycine's two H atoms shows why it alone is achiral. Step text only names what the canvas already showed, and Forms seen counts progress.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting distractors: NH2 on the carbon furthest from COOH (disproved by the build step), ethan- as alanine's stem (disproved when the name picker counts the COOH carbon as C1), every alpha-amino acid chiral (disproved by glycine), and alanine uncharged near pH 6 (disproved when the slider shows H3N+-CHR-COO- across pH 2.3 to 9.7).

challenge_feedback.evidence: The rotating challenge reuses thirteen tailored feedback lines that each name the error made: beta for alpha, OH for NH2, the R group mistaken for a constant group, the uncounted COOH carbon, numbering from C1 wrongly, serine called achiral, the anion picked in acid, the zwitterion picked at pH 1 and the alpha-carbon confused with the COOH or side-chain carbon.

readability.evidence: Learner text reads at FK 3.5 and adult text at FK 7.8, both inside the 6.5 and 9.5 learner targets, with short sentences that still carry the exact specification terms: alpha-amino acid, R group, zwitterion, optical isomers, chiral centre, IUPAC name and amine and carboxylic acid functional groups. Canvas labels are formulas or two to five words.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler patterns and 12% duplicate gate including against the Amines as bases and nucleophiles lesson. Each paragraph adds one idea (the general formula, naming from the COOH carbon, chirality and glycine, acid-base behaviour); the adult text names the common mistake of leaving the COOH carbon out of the count (aminoethanoic acid for alanine) and how to run the lab in a lesson.

mobile.evidence: Reviewed 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of all six steps: the tetrahedral sketch with question-mark bonds, the six fragment chips in one row above the hint, the glycine chirality card, the pH bar with 0 and 14 end labels and thumb, and the challenge formula card all fit with no clipping; the fragment buttons wrap to two rows. phone_sweep reported 0 findings.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passes Show me for every task on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge renders, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in light and dark themes and there are no console errors. Every canvas gesture has a button route (part buttons, plus-fragment buttons, name buttons, Chiral and Not chiral, pH -1 and pH +1) and the canvas aria-label is updated with each result.
